html:
Ferdinand II was King of Aragon from 1479 to 1516 and, with his wife Isabella I of Castile, one of the "Catholic Monarchs" who joined their kingdoms into what became Spain.

He married Isabella in 1469, against the wishes of her half-brother the king. When each inherited a crown, they ruled together, though Castile and Aragon kept their own laws, courts and coins. Their joint reign changed Spain and the world:

  • In 1478 they set up the Spanish Inquisition under royal control.
  • In 1492 they conquered Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia, and ordered the Jews to convert or leave.
  • The same year they backed Columbus's voyage west.

Ferdinand was the more worldly partner. He fought France in Italy and won the kingdom of Naples in 1504. After Isabella died that year, Castile passed to their daughter Joanna and her husband, and from 1507 Ferdinand ruled it again as her regent. In 1512 he approved the Laws of Burgos on the treatment of Native people in the Americas, and seized most of Navarre. Machiavelli held him up in The Prince as a model of a crafty new prince. His grandson Charles inherited all his lands and became the emperor Charles V.
